recipes.title: French Onion Soup
ingredients: 3/4 cup dry white wine (Chardonnay or Pinto Grigio)
steps: Slice the onions into strings of medium-size. They'll shrink down and you don't want them too thin. (Using a mandoline slicer makes this much easier)
Melt the butter in a large (4-5 quart) soup pot or dutch oven over medium-low heat.
Add the onions and use tongs to toss and coat them in the butter. Leave them uncovered as they cook.

The onions will caramelize slowly, this takes patience. 6 large onions could take over an hour to fully caramelize. Stir the onions every 20 minutes or so until they've reached your desired size and color.
Add the white wine, increase the heat to medium, and cook for an additional 2-3 minutes.
Pour in the beef and chicken broth and add the bay leaves and thyme.
Simmer for another 45 minutes, with the lid cracked.
While the soup simmers, preheat the oven to 350 degrees.
Slice the baguette into 1/2 inch thick slices. Brush the tops with olive oil if desired. Plan on using 1-2 slices per bowl depending on the width of the bread and the bowls you are using.
Increase the oven temperature to a low broil.
Top each baguette with cheese and bake in the oven until the cheese melts and begins to bubble and brown slightly.
Remove the bay leaves and thyme stems.
Ladle the warm soup into each bowl and use tongs to top each of them with the warm baguettes. Top with thyme if desired and serve!

recipes.title: Eds Nashville Hot Chicken Nuggets
ingredients: 6 lb thin-cut chicken breasts (cut into nuggets or small cubes)
16 tbsp cayenne pepper (for Nashville Hot seasoning)
8 tbsp light brown sugar (packed, for Nashville Hot seasoning)
8 tsp black pepper (freshly ground, for Nashville Hot seasoning)
6 tsp sea salt (for Nashville Hot seasoning)
4 tsp garlic powder (for Nashville Hot Seasoning)
steps: Brine the chicken: Place cubed chicken in pickle juice and milk (from brine ingredients). Cover and refrigerate for 4-24 hours.
Season the chicken: Remove chicken from brine. Lay pieces on a wire rack. Sprinkle Nashville seasoning evenly over the chicken. Flip and repeat. Let sit 5 minutes.
Coat the chicken - Step 1: Toss seasoned chicken in Bowl 1 (flour/seasoning mix).
Coat the chicken - Step 2: Dip into Bowl 2 (egg wash).
Coat the chicken - Step 3: Press firmly into Bowl 3 (panko mix).
Coat the chicken - Step 4: Place coated pieces on a rack and rest 10-15 minutes (to improve crust adhesion).
Fry the chicken: Heat oil to 350-360ºF. Fry in small batches for 4-6 minutes, until golden and chicken reaches 165ºF internal temperature.
Drain on a wire rack.

recipes.title: Bacon-Wrapped Smoked Hot Dog Bites
steps: Cut each hot dog into 4 equal pieces.
Place the hot-dog pieces in a bowl and add honey mustard and BBQ seasoning. Toss to coat evenly.
Cut the entire pack of bacon into fourths.
Wrap each hot-dog piece with one bacon quarter, keeping the bacon in a single layer so it renders properly.
Insert a toothpick through each piece to secure the bacon.
Preheat smoker to 250°F.
Arrange the bites on a wire rack or directly on the smoker grate.
Smoke for 60-90 minutes, or until the bacon is rendered and reaches your preferred crispness.
Optional: Brush with BBQ sauce during the last 10 minutes for a glaze.

recipes.title: Bacon, Cheddar Jalapeno Popper Pinwheels
ingredients: 1 can Crescent Rolls (or dough sheet, if you can find it)
1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese (1/4 cup reserved)
steps: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Mix cream cheese, bacon, jalapenos and garlic salt together in a small bowl and set aside.
Roll out crescent roll dough and lightly press seams together to form a sheet. (alternatively, you could use a rolled out pizza dough or a crescent dough sheet).
Layer ingredients evenly on the dough, sprinkle with cheese reserving about a few tablespoons for topping, and roll lengthwise.
Using a sharp, serrated knife, cut into 1-inch slices and place 2-inches apart on a foil lined cookie sheet. Top with reserved shredded cheddar, if desired.
Bake for 9-11 minutes, or until bread begins to brown. Oven temperatures can vary, so do use this time as a guideline.
Allow to cool slightly before plating and serving.

recipes.title: Bacon Fried Green Beans with Brown Sugar Bourbon Pecans
steps: Preheat your Blackstone to medium heat. Place 6 strips of thick cut bacon on the griddle and cook until crispy. Remove the bacon to paper towels to drain, but DO NOT remove the bacon fat from the griddle.
While the bacon is cooking, remove the small stems from your fresh green beans.
Add the green beans to the bacon fat on the griddle. Season with Kosher Salt and Coarse Black Pepper. Toss and allow to cook for 4 to 5 minutes total, ensuring they are not overcooked.
While the beans are cooking, chop the honey glazed pecans into small pieces.

When the beans are about 80% done, create a space in the middle of the green beans. Add 1/4 C of brown sugar and 1/4 C of bourbon of your choice. (Optional: Carefully light the bourbon with a lighter to cook off the alcohol faster).
When the fire has died down (after about 10 seconds), add the unsalted butter, chopped pecans, and craisins to the griddle.
Toss everything together until all ingredients are coated and the brown sugar has turned into a caramel consistency.
To plate, add the ingredients to a serving bowl and dust with Blackstone Sweet Maple seasoning. Enjoy!

recipes.title: Bacon Fried Corn 3.0
steps: Preheat your griddle top on low heat.
Add the diced pancetta to the griddle and let it slowly cook to gently render the fat without cooking it too fast. Toss the pancetta occasionally to brown all sides.
While the pancetta cooks, dice 2 tomatoes and mince half a red onion.
When the pancetta starts to brown, you can increase the heat to medium if necessary.
While the pancetta finishes cooking, chop up your fresh basil and parsley (the amount is based on preference).
Once the pancetta is done cooking, leaving all the rendered fat on the griddle, add the frozen corn.
Toss and coat the corn with the pancetta fat and season with salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
Add the Blackstone All-Purpose Seasoning. Toss and incorporate all seasonings.
Add the diced tomatoes, minced red onion, fresh basil, and parsley to the griddle top.
Toss everything together with the corn and pancetta.
Plate the mixture in a large dish, garnish with grated parmesan, and enjoy.

recipes.title: Bacon Bourbon Jell-O Shots
steps: In a large bowl or liquid measuring cup, sprinkle gelatin over bourbon and let bloom 5 minutes.
In a small saucepan over medium heat bring apple juice and sugar to a boil. Whisk boiling apple juice into gelatin mixture.
Cut bacon slices into thirds and place each third into shot glasses then pour jell-o mixture in.
Refrigerate until set, 2 hours.

recipes.title: Bacon Asparagus Brie Bites
steps: Arrange a rack in center of oven; preheat to 350°. In a large skillet over medium heat, cook bacon, turning occasionally, until crispy, about 8 minutes. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plate. Drain all but 2 Tbsp. fat from skillet.

Add asparagus to skillet and cook, turning occasionally, until bright green and only slightly tender, 2 to 3 minutes; season with salt and pepper. Squeeze lemon juice over, then transfer asparagus to a cutting board. Chop bacon and asparagus into bite-size pieces.
Cut brie into small square pieces, about 1” wide.
On a lightly floured surface, roll crescent dough to a 6” x 4” rectangle. If there are perforated edges, pinch together seams to seal. Cut dough into 24 (1” x 1”) squares.
Grease a 24-cup mini muffin tin with cooking spray. Place a square into each muffin cup. Fill with brie, bacon, and asparagus.
Bake bites until dough is golden brown, about 10 minutes.

recipes.title: Au Jus Recipe (Made With or Without Drippings)
ingredients: 4 tablespoons red wine (or low-sodium beef broth)
4 tablespoons red wine (or low-sodium beef broth)
1/2 teaspoon salt (more or less to taste)
steps: Place medium saucepan on stovetop over high heat. When saucepan is warm, add 4 tablespoons beef drippings, 4 tablespoons red wine, 2 cups low-sodium beef broth, and 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce.
Whisk ingredients together until incorporated, then bring mixture to boil. Once mixture begins to boil, reduce heat under saucepan to medium-low. Simmer mixture 5 minutes.

After 5 minutes, taste mixture and add salt and freshly cracked black pepper to taste. When satisfied with flavor, transfer jus into serving container. Note: if your drippings contained any remnants from the beef, strain the jus through a fine mesh sieve first, so you're left with a smooth liquid.
Serve warm with prime rib, French dip sandwiches, roast beef, or other meal as desired.

Place medium saucepan on stovetop over high heat. When saucepan is warm, add 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, 4 tablespoons red wine, 2 cups low-sodium beef broth, 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce, ½ teaspoon onion powder, and ½ teaspoon garlic powder.
Whisk ingredients together until incorporated, then bring mixture to boil. Once mixture begins to boil, reduce heat under saucepan to medium-low. Simmer mixture 5 minutes.
After 5 minutes, taste mixture and add ½ teaspoon salt, onion powder, and/or garlic as desired. When satisfied with flavor, transfer au jus into serving container.
Serve warm with prime rib, French dip sandwiches, roast beef, or other meal as desired.

recipes.title: Applebee's Style 3 Cheese Chicken Penne
ingredients: 8 ounces Italian cheese (shredded, Mozzarella, Parmesan, Provolone)
steps: Chop Chicken and marinade in Italian dressing for 30 minute.
Chop tomatoes, add oil chopped Garlic and basil to make bruschetta. Set aside.
Cook Penne in boiling water.
Grill or broil Chicken.
Divide pasta between two microwavable bowls.
Pour Alfredo sauce.over the pasta in each bowl.
Layer on Bruschetta.
Add a layer of Chicken.
Add a layer of shredded cheese.
Microwave for 3 min, or longer if previously chilled till cheese is melted.
Serve with Garlic bread.
Can be prepared well ahead of time in individual bowls, then Microwaved thoroughly.

NB. I have edited this recipe from the original post. Thanks to JFitz who kindly pointed out I had omitted to include the Garlic in the Bruschetta. JFitz also added the that she cooked the meal in a casserole dish, in the oven. I have done this successfully also, but I have failed at it by using low quality shredded Italian 3 cheese mix. Always use fresh.

recipes.title: 5 Ingredient Parmesan Garlic Penne
steps: Cook penne pasta according to package direction then drain and set aside.
In a medium pot melt your butter and sauté garlic whisking until butter has started to become golden brown. Add basil and continue to whisk.
Add cooked pasta to your pot and toss until coated. Add grated parmesan cheese and toss until coated.

recipes.title: Dirt Cake
ingredients: 8 oz whipped topping (frozen, such as Cool Whip, thawed)
1 1/2 cup sandwich cookies (crushed, such as Oreos)
steps: Whisk together milk and instant pudding for 2 minutes, until pudding is completely dissolved, and let stand 5 minutes to thicken.
Stir in frozen whipped topping and 1/2 cup of crushed cookies.
Spoon into 10 cups.
Sprinkle remaining crushed cookies over the pudding mixture.
Top each cup with 2 gummy worms.
Chill until ready to serve, then enjoy.

recipes.title: Buttered Noodles
steps: Cook the noodles according to package directions until al dente.
Drain the noodles well.
Return the hot noodles to the pot.
Add the butter and salt.
Toss gently until the butter is melted and the noodles are evenly coated.
Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Blackstone Whiskey Burger with Jalapeno and Bacon
ingredients: 1 serving Blackstone Whiskey Burger Seasoning (to taste)
steps: Cook bacon until crispy.
Crumble the crispy bacon.
Remove seeds from jalapenos and dice them.
In a medium-sized bowl, combine the ground beef, crumbled bacon, shredded cheddar cheese, and diced jalapeno. Mix thoroughly with your hands.
Divide the mixture into 4 equal portions and form into patties.
Liberally season the outside of both sides of the hamburgers with Blackstone Whiskey Burger Seasoning.
Cook the burgers on a grill, cast iron skillet, or flat top until desired doneness is reached.
Optional: Top with Hellfire salt before serving.

recipes.title: Bacon-Wrapped Smoked Hot Dog Bites
steps: Cut each hot dog into 4 equal pieces.
Place the hot-dog pieces in a bowl and add honey mustard and BBQ seasoning. Toss to coat evenly.
Cut the entire pack of bacon into fourths.
Wrap each hot-dog piece with one bacon quarter, keeping the bacon in a single layer so it renders properly.
Insert a toothpick through each piece to secure the bacon.
Preheat smoker to 250°F.
Arrange the bites on a wire rack or directly on the smoker grate.
Smoke for 60-90 minutes, or until the bacon is rendered and reaches your preferred crispness.
Optional: Brush with BBQ sauce during the last 10 minutes for a glaze.

recipes.title: 321 Ribs
steps: Preheat. Prepare your smoker by preheating it to 180 degrees F.

Prep the ribs. Use a sharp knife to lift up the corner of the membrane on the back of the ribs. Using a paper towel, grip the membrane and pull firmly to fully remove the membrane. Trim any excess fat off the ribs as needed.
Season. Liberally season both sides of the ribs using Hey Grill Hey Sweet Rub, starting with the bone side.

Smoke. Place the seasoned ribs on the smoker and close the lid. Leave them to smoke for 3 hours (The ribs should be somewhere around an internal temperature of 165 degrees F at the end of these 3 hours).

Make the braise. Tear off a large piece of aluminum foil and place it on a large working surface. Transfer the ribs to the foil bone side up so the bones don't tear through the foil. Sprinkle the ribs with the brown sugar, top with the butter cut into small pads, and then pour in the apple cider. Tightly crimp the foil together to create an airtight seal.
Continue smoking. Return the wrapped ribs to the grill and increase the temperature in the smoker to 225 degrees F. Let the ribs braise for 2 hours in the foil.

Sauce. Carefully remove the ribs from the grill and place them on a large working surface. Open the foil package (be careful of hot steam) and use tongs to remove the ribs and place them back on the grill, bone side down. Discard the foil and excess cooking liquid. Next, brush the ribs with Everything BBQ Sauce (or your favorite BBQ sauce).

Finish smoking. Return the unwrapped, sauced ribs to the smoker. Close the lid, and continue smoking for an hour (or less!) or until the ribs reach around 200 degrees F and the sauce is sticky and set.
Rest, slice, and enjoy. Remove the ribs from the smoker and rest for 10-15 minutes. Slice into individual ribs, and serve with extra sauce, as desired.

recipes.title: "Elevated" Buttered Noodles
steps: Boil your pasta in heavily salted water, aiming for 2 minutes before the package says "al dente." The pasta will finish cooking in the sauce.

While the pasta boils, melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a wide skillet over medium-low heat. If desired, let the butter foam and turn a light nut-brown (Beurre Noisette) before turning the heat to low.
Use tongs to transfer the noodles directly from the pot to the skillet. It’s okay if some water hitches a ride.
Add about 1/4 cup of pasta water and the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter to the skillet.
Increase the heat to medium and toss vigorously until a creamy sauce forms.
Turn off the heat. Sprinkle in the Parmesan and keep tossing until the sauce is silky. If it looks dry, add another splash of pasta water.
Fold in the fresh parsley and a squeeze of lemon to cut through the richness.
Finish with flaky salt and black pepper.

recipes.title: Pit Boss Smoked Chicken Breast Burnt Ends
recipes.description: The brisket burnt end treatment applied to chicken — cubed breasts smoked twice and tossed in a sticky chipotle-bourbon BBQ sauce until caramelized and addictive.
ingredients: 2 tbsp chipotle peppers in adobo, minced
steps: Cube and season chicken: Mix chipotle powder, cayenne pepper, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, brown sugar, kosher salt, and black pepper together. Cube chicken breasts into 1.5-inch pieces, toss with olive oil, then coat thoroughly in the dry rub.
Preheat smoker: Preheat your Pit Boss to 225°F with hickory or peach pellets. Arrange cubed chicken in a single layer directly on the grates or on a wire rack.
First smoke: Smoke chicken cubes at 225°F for 1.5 hours until they develop a good bark and reach an internal temp of 165°F.

Make chipotle-bourbon sauce: While chicken smokes, combine BBQ sauce, chipotle peppers in adobo, bourbon, honey, and butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir until butter melts and sauce is glossy, about 5 minutes.
Sauce the burnt ends: Transfer smoked chicken cubes to a disposable aluminum pan. Pour chipotle-bourbon sauce over the top and toss to coat every piece generously.
Second smoke: Return the pan uncovered to the smoker at 225°F for another 45–60 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the sauce caramelizes and the edges get sticky and slightly crispy.
Rest and serve: Pull from the smoker and let rest 5 minutes. Serve straight from the pan with extra sauce on the side.
recipes.notes: Don't skip the second smoke — that's what creates the sticky, caramelized exterior that makes burnt ends so special. These are incredible served over white bread or buttered Texas toast to soak up the sauce. Peach or cherry pellets add a nice sweetness that plays off the chipotle heat perfectly.

recipes.title: Pit Boss Cayenne-Brined Smoked Chicken Breast Sandwiches
recipes.description: Nashville hot chicken meets the pellet smoker — spicy buttermilk-brined breasts smoked low and slow, piled on brioche with comeback sauce and crispy slaw.
steps: Brine the chicken: Whisk together buttermilk, cayenne pepper, kosher salt, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and brown sugar in a large bowl or zip-lock bag. Add chicken breasts, submerge fully, and refrigerate.
Make comeback sauce: Stir together mayonnaise, hot sauce, Dijon mustard, and garlic powder in a small bowl. Refrigerate until serving.
Make spicy slaw: Toss coleslaw mix with apple cider vinegar, cayenne pepper, and sugar. Season with salt, toss well, and refrigerate so the slaw softens slightly.
Preheat smoker: Fire up your Pit Boss to 225°F using hickory or competition blend pellets. Let it come fully up to temp before adding chicken.
Smoke the chicken: Remove chicken from brine, pat dry, and place directly on the grates. Smoke at 225°F until internal temp reaches 165°F, approximately 1.5–2 hours.
Rest and assemble: Rest chicken 5–10 minutes, then slice or serve whole on toasted brioche buns with a generous spread of comeback sauce and a heap of spicy slaw on top.
recipes.notes: For extra heat, dust the brined chicken with an additional pinch of cayenne right before it hits the smoker. Toast your brioche buns cut-side down on the smoker grates for the last 5 minutes of the cook for incredible flavor. Cherry pellets work beautifully here as an alternative to hickory for a slightly sweeter smoke.

recipes.title: Smoked Tri-Tip with Coffee-Ancho Rub
recipes.description: Tri-tip is the hidden gem of the smoker — lean, beefy, and incredibly flavorful without the price tag of tenderloin or the fat of brisket. This coffee-ancho dry rub brings a bold, smoky-sweet depth with mild heat that's totally new territory from your classic steakhouse flavors. Smoked low and slow over oak or cherry wood, then reverse-seared for a perfect crust.
ingredients: 1 tri-tip roast (2.5 to 3 lbs), fat cap trimmed
2 tbsp finely ground dark roast coffee
Oak or cherry wood chunks for smoking
steps: Trim the tri-tip of any thick fat cap, leaving just a very thin layer for moisture. Pat completely dry with paper towels.
Combine the ground coffee, ancho chili powder, smoked paprika, salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, brown sugar, and cayenne in a small bowl. Mix well.

Rub the tri-tip all over with the neutral oil, then coat evenly and generously with the dry rub on all sides, pressing it in firmly. Let the roast rest at room temperature for 45–60 minutes before cooking.
Prepare your smoker for indirect heat at 225°F. Add 2–3 wood chunks of oak or cherry wood for a medium, slightly sweet smoke profile.
Place the tri-tip on the smoker grate over indirect heat, fat-side up. Insert a leave-in meat thermometer into the thickest part.
Smoke at 225°F until the internal temperature reaches 120–125°F for medium-rare, approximately 1.5 to 2 hours depending on thickness. Avoid opening the smoker frequently.
Once the target temp is reached, remove the tri-tip and tent loosely with foil. Increase your smoker or a cast iron skillet to high heat (450–500°F) for the reverse sear.
Sear the tri-tip 1–2 minutes per side over high heat until a dark, caramelized crust forms and internal temp hits 130–135°F for medium-rare.
Rest the roast uncovered on a cutting board for 10–12 minutes. This is critical — do not skip this step.
Tri-tip has two grain directions that meet in the middle. Identify where they change and slice each section against the grain into 0.25-inch slices. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Ed's Parmesan Crusted Bruschetta Chicken
steps: Pound chicken breasts thin to an even thickness.
In a shallow dish, mix the grated parmesan with the panko, aiming for a ratio of roughly 2 parts panko to 1 part parmesan.
Set up a dredging station: one dish with flour, one dish with beaten eggs, and the third dish with the panko mixture.
Dip each chicken breast first in flour, shaking off excess, then dip in egg, and finally coat thoroughly in the panko mixture.
Fry the crusted chicken in oil over medium-high heat. Use a press or spatula to ensure good contact and a crispy coat on both sides until cooked through.
Prepare the bruschetta topping: Dice tomatoes (assuming tomatoes are an implied ingredient based on 'Bruschetta' and 'Dice tomatoes'), dice the red onion, and place them in a bowl.
Add olive oil (estimated quantity: 3 tbsp) to the bowl with the diced vegetables.
Add garlic powder, chopped basil, salt, and pepper to the bowl.
Mix the bruschetta ingredients well.
Place a generous amount of shaved parmesan on top of the cooked chicken breasts.
Spoon the prepared bruschetta mixture over the shaved parmesan topping.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions. Drain and toss with butter.
Serve the Parmesan Crusted Bruschetta Chicken over the buttered spaghetti noodles.

recipes.title: Parmesan Crust for Steaks
ingredients: 1 tsp shredded mozzarella (optional, estimate based on '1 - 2 teaspoon extra if you want')
1 tsp olive oil (for extra, keeps it from solidifying too fast)
3 drop lemon juice (for brightness, optional but excellent)
1 pinch parsley (for color, optional but excellent)
steps: Combine the main ingredients: Parmesan, panko, softened butter, softened cream cheese, garlic powder, onion powder, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper.
If using optional ingredients, combine the extra butter, minced garlic, olive oil, salt, Italian seasoning, lemon juice, and parsley.
Divide the main mixture into generous mounds.
Press each mound onto the top of each steak.
Broil for 1-2 minutes until the crust is golden and bubbling.

recipes.title: Classic Steakhouse Mustard Sauce
ingredients: 1 tsp maple syrup (agave, treacle or honey (optional))
1 tbsp tarragon (chopped, any herb of your choice will work, finely)
steps: After you reverse sear your steak in a smoking hot pan, turn the heat off to let it cool a bit (about 5-6 minutes) and not burn the ingredients.
Add the butter and shallots and turn the heat back on to maintain medium high heat.
Sauté the shallots until translucent (about 4-5 minutes).
Add your alcohol carefully so as not to flame (although some people do this to cook off the alcohol). Cook for 3-4 minutes or until the alcohol has reduced by half.
Add the heavy cream and your maple, honey or other sweetener and let this come to a low simmer. Watch carefully as it may bubble over.
Reduce the liquid by a third or until the mixture coats the back of a spoon. It should be the texture of pancake batter.
Off the heat but while the mixture is still hot, whisk in the mustard until thoroughly combined.
Stir in the tarragon.
If you seasoned your steak well, that salt and pepper will have infused your mixture, but taste for seasoning and add.
